246	class _Case(_Expr):
247	    """A searched CASE: ordered (condition, result) branches and an ELSE."""
248	
249	    __slots__ = ("branches", "else_node")
250	
251	    def __init__(self, branches: tuple, else_node: _Expr | None, type_name: str):
252	        children = tuple(
253	            child for condition, result in branches for child in (condition, result)
254	        )
255	        if else_node is not None:
256	            children += (else_node,)
257	        nullable = else_node is None or any(
258	            result.nullable for _condition, result in branches
259	        ) or (else_node is not None and else_node.nullable)
260	        super().__init__(type_name, nullable, children)
261	        self.branches = branches
262	        self.else_node = else_node
263	
264	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
265	        # Written order is preserved; an omitted ELSE is rendered as null,
266	        # which also marks the implicit result nullable in the output schema.
267	        return {
268	            "kind": "case",
269	            "cases": [
270	                {"when": condition.to_json(), "then": result.to_json()}
271	                for condition, result in self.branches
272	            ],
273	            "else": None if self.else_node is None else self.else_node.to_json(),
274	        }
275	
276	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
277	        # Conditions are tried in written order; only TRUE matches.  FALSE
278	        # and UNKNOWN fall through, so unhit results are never evaluated:
279	        # their division-by-zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64
280	        # cannot raise.  The chosen result alone is evaluated.
281	        for condition, result in self.branches:
282	            if condition.eval(row, agg_values) is True:
283	                value = result.eval(row, agg_values)
284	                break
285	        else:
286	            value = (
287	                None
288	                if self.else_node is None
289	                else self.else_node.eval(row, agg_values)
290	            )
291	        if value is None:
292	            return None
293	        if self.type == "float64" and isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(
294	            value, bool
295	        ):
296	            return float(value)
297	        return value
298	
299	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
300	        # Each result expression is evaluated only on the sub-batch of rows
301	        # routed to it, so an error inside an unhit branch never raises;
302	        # rows no branch claimed fall through to ELSE (or NULL).
303	        result: list = [None] * len(batch)
304	        remaining = list(range(len(batch)))
305	        for condition, result_node in self.branches:
306	            if not remaining:
307	                break
308	            cond_values = condition.eval_batch(
309	                source_columns, [batch[k] for k in remaining], agg_values
310	            )
311	            taken = [k for k, cond in zip(remaining, cond_values) if cond is True]
312	            remaining = [
313	                k for k, cond in zip(remaining, cond_values) if cond is not True
314	            ]
315	            if taken:
316	                values = result_node.eval_batch(
317	                    source_columns, [batch[k] for k in taken], agg_values
318	                )
319	                for k, value in zip(taken, values):
320	                    result[k] = value
321	        if remaining and self.else_node is not None:
322	            values = self.else_node.eval_batch(
323	                source_columns, [batch[k] for k in remaining], agg_values
324	            )
325	            for k, value in zip(remaining, values):
326	                result[k] = value
327	        if self.type == "float64":
328	            # int64/float64 results unify to float64; ints become floats.
329	            return [self._unify_float(value) for value in result]
330	        return result
331	
332	    @staticmethod
333	    def _unify_float(value):
334	        if value is None:
335	            return None
336	        # int64/float64 results unify to float64; ints become floats.
337	        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
338	            return float(value)
339	        return value

342	class _Predicate(_Expr):
343	    """Base class for the three-valued boolean conditions."""
344	
345	    __slots__ = ()
346	
347	    is_value = False
348	
349	    def __init__(self, nullable: bool, children: tuple = ()):
350	        super().__init__("bool", nullable, children)
351	
352	
353	class _Cmp(_Predicate):
354	    """A comparison of two value nodes (UNKNOWN when either side is NULL)."""
355	
356	    __slots__ = ("op", "left", "right")
357	
358	    def __init__(self, op: str, left: _Expr, right: _Expr):
359	        super().__init__(left.nullable or right.nullable, (left, right))
360	        self.op = op
361	        self.left = left
362	        self.right = right
363	
364	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
365	        return {
366	            "kind": "comparison",
367	            "operator": self.op,
368	            "operands": [self.left.to_json(), self.right.to_json()],
369	        }
370	
371	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
372	        left = self.left.eval(row, agg_values)
373	        right = self.right.eval(row, agg_values)
374	        if left is None or right is None:
375	            return None
376	        return _compare_values(self.op, left, right)
377	
378	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
379	        left = self.left.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
380	        right = self.right.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
381	        op = self.op
382	        return [
383	            None if lval is None or rval is None else _compare_values(op, lval, rval)
384	            for lval, rval in zip(left, right)
385	        ]
386	
387	
388	class _IsNull(_Predicate):
389	    """IS NULL / IS NOT NULL; never itself UNKNOWN."""
390	
391	    __slots__ = ("operand", "negated")
392	
393	    def __init__(self, operand: _Expr, negated: bool):
394	        super().__init__(False, (operand,))
395	        self.operand = operand
396	        self.negated = negated
397	
398	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
399	        return {
400	            "kind": "is_null",
401	            "operator": "IS NOT NULL" if self.negated else "IS NULL",
402	            "operands": [self.operand.to_json()],
403	        }
404	
405	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
406	        value = self.operand.eval(row, agg_values)
407	        result = value is None
408	        return not result if self.negated else result
409	
410	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
411	        values = self.operand.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
412	        if self.negated:  # IS NOT NULL
413	            return [value is not None for value in values]
414	        return [value is None for value in values]
415	
416	
417	class _Not(_Predicate):
418	    __slots__ = ("operand",)
419	
420	    def __init__(self, operand: _Expr):
421	        super().__init__(operand.nullable, (operand,))
422	        self.operand = operand
423	
424	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
425	        return {
426	            "kind": "not",
427	            "operator": "NOT",
428	            "operands": [self.operand.to_json()],
429	        }
430	
431	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
432	        value = self.operand.eval(row, agg_values)
433	        return None if value is None else (not value)
434	
435	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
436	        values = self.operand.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
437	        return [None if value is None else (not value) for value in values]
438	
439	
440	class _Logic(_Predicate):
441	    """AND / OR; UNKNOWN propagates through either side."""
442	
443	    __slots__ = ("op", "left", "right")
444	
445	    def __init__(self, op: str, left: _Expr, right: _Expr):
446	        super().__init__(left.nullable or right.nullable, (left, right))
447	        self.op = op
448	        self.left = left
449	        self.right = right
450	
451	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
452	        return {
453	            "kind": "logic",
454	            "operator": self.op.upper(),
455	            "operands": [self.left.to_json(), self.right.to_json()],
456	        }
457	
458	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
459	        # Short-circuit SQL semantics; UNKNOWN propagates only when needed.
460	        left = self.left.eval(row, agg_values)
461	        if self.op == "and":
462	            if left is False:
463	                return False
464	            right = self.right.eval(row, agg_values)
465	            if right is False:
466	                return False
467	            if left is None or right is None:
468	                return None
469	            return True
470	        if left is True:
471	            return True
472	        right = self.right.eval(row, agg_values)
473	        if right is True:
474	            return True
475	        if left is None or right is None:
476	            return None
477	        return False
478	
479	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
480	        left = self.left.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
481	        # Rows the left operand already decided (FALSE for AND, TRUE for
482	        # OR) never evaluate the right operand, exactly as row-wise
483	        # short-circuiting; the rest form the sub-batch evaluated next.
484	        if self.op == "and":
485	            undecided = [k for k, value in enumerate(left) if value is not False]
486	        else:
487	            undecided = [k for k, value in enumerate(left) if value is not True]
488	        result = list(left)
489	        if undecided:
490	            right = self.right.eval_batch(
491	                source_columns,
492	                [batch[k] for k in undecided],
493	                agg_values,
494	            )
495	            for k, rval in zip(undecided, right):
496	                lval = left[k]
497	                if self.op == "and":
498	                    result[k] = (
499	                        False
500	                        if rval is False
501	                        else (None if lval is None or rval is None else True)
502	                    )
503	                else:
504	                    result[k] = (
505	                        True
506	                        if rval is True
507	                        else (None if lval is None or rval is None else False)
508	                    )
509	        return result
510	
511	
512	def _bind_expr(node: tuple, schema: Schema) -> _Expr:
513	    tag = node[0]
514	    if tag == "literal":
515	        return _Literal(node[1], node[2])
516	    if tag == "column":
517	        name = node[1]
518	        try:
519	            index = schema.index(name)
520	        except KeyError:
521	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
522	        col = schema.columns[index]
523	        return _Column(name, index, col.type, col.nullable)
524	    if tag == "not":
525	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
526	        _require_boolean(operand, "NOT")
527	        return _Not(operand)
528	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
529	        left = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
530	        right = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
531	        _require_boolean(left, tag.upper())
532	        _require_boolean(right, tag.upper())
533	        return _Logic(tag, left, right)
534	    if tag == "isnull":
535	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
536	        if not operand.is_value:
537	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
538	                "IS NULL operand must be a column reference or a literal"
539	            )
540	        return _IsNull(operand, node[2])
541	    if tag == "unary":
542	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
543	        type_name = operand.type
544	        if type_name not in ("int64", "float64"):
545	            raise QueryValidationError(
546	                f"unary +/- requires a numeric operand, got {type_name}"
547	            )
548	        return _Unary(operand, node[2])
549	    if tag == "arith":
550	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
551	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
552	        left_t = left.type
553	        right_t = right.type
554	        if left_t not in ("int64", "float64") or right_t not in ("int64", "float64"):
555	            raise QueryValidationError(
556	                f"arithmetic requires numeric operands, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
557	            )
558	        op = node[1]
559	        out_type = (
560	            "float64"
561	            if op == "/" or "float64" in (left_t, right_t)
562	            else "int64"
563	        )
564	        return _Arith(op, left, right, out_type)
565	    if tag == "case":
566	        bound_branches = []
567	        result_types: list[str] = []
568	        for cond_node, result_node in node[1]:
569	            cond = _bind_expr(cond_node, schema)
570	            _require_boolean(cond, "WHEN")
571	            result = _bind_expr(result_node, schema)
572	            bound_branches.append((cond, result))
573	            result_types.append(result.type)
574	        else_bound = None
575	        if node[2] is not None:
576	            else_bound = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
577	            result_types.append(else_bound.type)
578	        out_type = _unify_case_types(result_types)
579	        return _Case(tuple(bound_branches), else_bound, out_type)
580	    if tag == "cmp":
581	        op = node[1]
582	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
583	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
584	        if not (left.is_value and right.is_value):
585	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
586	                "comparison operands must be column references or literals"
587	            )
588	        _check_comparison_types(op, left, right)
589	        return _Cmp(op, left, right)
590	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive
591	
592	
593	def _check_comparison_types(op: str, left: _Expr, right: _Expr) -> None:
594	    """Validate the static operand types of one comparison (WHERE and HAVING)."""
595	    left_t = left.type
596	    right_t = right.type
597	    if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
598	        if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
599	            raise QueryValidationError(
600	                f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
601	            )
602	        if op not in ("=", "!="):
603	            raise QueryValidationError(f"bool only supports = and !=, not {op!r}")
604	    elif "utf8" in (left_t, right_t):
605	        if left_t != "utf8" or right_t != "utf8":
606	            raise QueryValidationError(
607	                f"utf8 can only be compared to utf8, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
608	            )
609	    elif not {left_t, right_t} <= {"int64", "float64"}:
610	        raise QueryValidationError(
611	            f"cannot compare values of type {left_t} and {right_t}"
612	        )
613	
614	
615	def _unify_case_types(types: list[str]) -> str:
616	    """Unify the static types of every reachable CASE result.
617	
618	    int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64; bool and utf8 must
619	    match every other result exactly.  Anything else is incompatible.
620	    """
621	    unique = set(types)
622	    if unique <= {"int64", "float64"}:
623	        return "float64" if "float64" in unique else "int64"
624	    if len(unique) == 1:
625	        return next(iter(unique))
626	    raise QueryValidationError(
627	        "CASE results must have consistent types: "
628	        + ", ".join(sorted(unique))
629	    )
630	
631	
632	def _require_boolean(node: _Expr, context: str) -> None:
633	    if node.type != "bool":
634	        raise QueryValidationError(
635	            f"{context} requires a boolean operand, got {node.type}"
636	        )
637	
638	
639	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
640	# Three-valued-logic evaluation
641	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
642	#
643	# The per-row semantics live on the bound expression nodes themselves
644	# (:meth:`_Expr.eval`); a batch failure falls back to that same row-at-a-
645	# time method (see :func:`_eval_batch`) so the reported first error keeps
646	# its historical row order.  The batched semantics
647	# (:meth:`_Expr.eval_batch`) visit exactly the same
648	# (row, subexpression) pairs.
649	
650	
651	def _compare_values(op: str, left, right) -> bool:
652	    """The boolean result of one comparison on two non-NULL values."""
653	    if op == "=":
654	        result = left == right
655	    elif op == "!=":
656	        result = left != right
657	    elif op == "<":
658	        result = left < right
659	    elif op == "<=":
660	        result = left <= right
661	    elif op == ">":
662	        result = left > right
663	    else:  # ">="
664	        result = left >= right
665	    return bool(result)
666	
667	
668	def _negate_value(value):
669	    # Unary minus: the type is preserved; only int64 can overflow.
670	    if isinstance(value, int):
671	        if value == _INT64_MIN:
672	            raise QueryValidationError(
673	                "negating the int64 minimum overflows the int64 range"
674	            )
675	        return -value
676	    return -value
677	
678	
679	def _arith_value(op: str, left, right):
680	    # int64 op int64 stays int64 for + - *; any float64 operand or a
681	    # division produces float64.  NULLs are handled by the caller.
682	    if op == "/" or isinstance(left, float) or isinstance(right, float):
683	        if op == "/" and right == 0:
684	            raise QueryValidationError("division by zero")
685	        a = float(left)
686	        b = float(right)
687	        if op == "+":
688	            result = a + b
689	        elif op == "-":
690	            result = a - b
691	        elif op == "*":
692	            result = a * b
693	        else:
694	            result = a / b
695	        if not math.isfinite(result):
696	            raise QueryValidationError(
697	                "float64 arithmetic produced a non-finite value"
698	            )
699	        return result
700	    if op == "+":
701	        result = left + right
702	    elif op == "-":
703	        result = left - right
704	    else:
705	        result = left * right
706	    if not (_INT64_MIN <= result <= _INT64_MAX):
707	        raise QueryValidationError("int64 arithmetic overflowed the int64 range")
708	    return result
709	
710	
711	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
712	# Batched column-vector evaluation
713	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
714	#
715	# The row-processing stages -- the WHERE filter, the ORDER BY sort keys,
716	# the SELECT expressions and the projection feeding SELECT DISTINCT -- share
717	# one batched evaluator.  Each stage hands the next a set of valid row
718	# indices; an expression is evaluated one *batch* of rows at a time against
719	# the source columns and yields one vector of result values aligned with
720	# the batch, instead of re-entering the row-at-a-time control flow for
721	# every row.  The vectorised walk is the node's own ``eval_batch``; its
722	# semantics are exactly those of :meth:`_Expr.eval` (NULL propagation,
723	# three-valued logic, per-row CASE short-circuit, the int64 / float64
724	# error rules).  Because the batched walk visits the same
725	# (row, subexpression) pairs as the row-wise walk, any batch that contains
726	# a failing row raises; the driver then re-runs that batch row by row so
727	# the reported error is byte-identical to the historical one.
728	
729	_EVAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2048
730	
731	
732	def _iter_batches(indices, size=_EVAL_BATCH_SIZE):
733	    """Yield ``indices`` sliced into consecutive batches of at most ``size``."""
734	    for start in range(0, len(indices), size):
735	        yield indices[start : start + size]
736	
737	
738	def _eval_batch(node: _Expr, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None = None) -> list:
739	    """Evaluate one batch of a bound expression, returning a value vector.
740	
741	    ``batch`` is the current valid-row set (row indices into
742	    ``source_columns``); the returned list holds one value per batch row, in
743	    batch order.  A :class:`QueryValidationError` anywhere in the batch is
744	    re-raised through the row-wise reference path so the exact historical
745	    error (and its row order) surfaces.
746	    """
747	    try:
748	        return node.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
749	    except QueryValidationError:
750	        # The batched walk visits the same (row, subexpression) pairs as
751	        # the row-wise one, so this re-run raises the same first error the
752	        # pre-vectorised engine reported for these rows.
753	        return [node.eval(_row_values(source_columns, i), agg_values) for i in batch]
754	
755	
756	def _eval_expr_selection(node, source_columns, selected) -> list:
757	    """Evaluate ``node`` over the row indices ``selected``, batch by batch.
758	
759	    Returns one list of values aligned with ``selected``; shared by the
760	    WHERE filter, the ORDER BY sort keys and the SELECT projections.
761	    """
762	    values: list = []
763	    for batch in _iter_batches(selected):
764	        values.extend(_eval_batch(node, source_columns, batch))
765	    return values
766	
767	
768	def _filter_rows(where: _Expr, source_columns, row_count: int) -> list[int]:
769	    """The row indices whose WHERE condition evaluates to TRUE.
770	
771	    Batched counterpart of the historical row loop: rows are evaluated
772	    batch by batch in file order, and FALSE and UNKNOWN both drop the row.
773	    """
774	    selected: list[int] = []
775	    for batch in _iter_batches(list(range(row_count))):
776	        mask = _eval_batch(where, source_columns, batch)
777	        selected.extend(i for i, keep in zip(batch, mask) if keep is True)
778	    return selected
779	def _row_values(source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...], i: int) -> tuple:
780	    return tuple(col[i] for col in source_columns)

1	"""Pure SQL parsing: tokeniser, parsed statement tree and the parser.
2	
3	This stage turns SQL text into a :class:`_Select` tree of plain tuples and
4	frozen data classes.  It is deliberately free of any file, schema, source
5	or join knowledge -- importing it never opens a file, and a
6	:class:`~columnar_analytics.errors.QuerySyntaxError` raised here always
7	surfaces before any source is read.  Later stages
8	(:mod:`columnar_analytics.resolve` for name resolution,
9	:mod:`columnar_analytics.binder` for schema binding) consume the parsed
10	tree; nothing here imports them.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import math
16	import re
17	from dataclasses import dataclass
18	from typing import Any
19	
20	from .errors import QuerySyntaxError, QueryValidationError
21	
22	
23	_KEYWORDS = frozenset(
24	    (
25	        "select",
26	        "distinct",
27	        "from",
28	        "where",
29	        "as",
30	        "not",
31	        "and",
32	        "or",
33	        "is",
34	        "null",
35	        "true",
36	        "false",
37	        "order",
38	        "by",
39	        "asc",
40	        "desc",
41	        "nulls",
42	        "first",
43	        "last",
44	        "limit",
45	        "group",
46	        "having",
47	        "inner",
48	        "left",
49	        "join",
50	        "on",
51	        "case",
52	        "when",
53	        "then",
54	        "else",
55	        "end",
56	    )
57	)
58	
59	# Aggregate function names are ordinary (case-insensitive) identifiers that
60	# gain call syntax only in the projection and ORDER BY.
61	_AGG_NAMES = frozenset(("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max"))
62	_INT64_MIN = -(2**63)
63	_INT64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	# Tokeniser
66	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
67	
68	
69	@dataclass(frozen=True)
70	class _Token:
71	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
72	    value: Any
73	    text: str
74	
75	
76	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
77	    r"""
78	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
79	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
80	    """,
81	    re.VERBOSE,
82	)
83	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
84	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
85	
86	
87	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
88	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
89	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
90	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
91	    i = 0
92	    n = len(sql)
93	    while i < n:
94	        ch = sql[i]
95	        if ch.isspace():
96	            i += 1
97	            continue
98	        if ch == "*":
99	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
100	            i += 1
101	            continue
102	        if ch in ",()+-/":
103	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
104	            i += 1
105	            continue
106	        if ch in "=<>!":
107	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
108	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
109	                i += 2
110	                continue
111	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
112	                op = ch + "="
113	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
114	                i += 2
115	                continue
116	            if ch in "=<>":
117	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
118	                i += 1
119	                continue
120	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
121	        if ch == "'":
122	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
123	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
124	            i = new_i
125	            continue
126	        if ch == '"':
127	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
128	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
129	            i = new_i
130	            continue
131	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
132	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
133	            if match:
134	                text = match.group(0)
135	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
136	                i = match.end()
137	                continue
138	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
139	            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
140	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
141	            i += 1
142	            continue
143	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
144	        if match:
145	            text = match.group(0)
146	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
147	            i = match.end()
148	            continue
149	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
150	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
151	    return tokens
152	
153	
154	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
155	    lowered = word.lower()
156	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
157	        if lowered == "true":
158	            return _Token("number", True, word)
159	        if lowered == "false":
160	            return _Token("number", False, word)
161	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
162	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
163	
164	
165	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
166	    parts: list[str] = []
167	    i = start + 1
168	    n = len(sql)
169	    while True:
170	        j = sql.find("'", i)
171	        if j == -1:
172	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
173	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
174	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
175	            parts.append("'")
176	            i = j + 2
177	            continue
178	        value = "".join(parts)
179	        try:
180	            value.encode("utf-8")
181	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
182	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
183	        return value, j + 1
184	
185	
186	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
187	    parts: list[str] = []
188	    i = start + 1
189	    n = len(sql)
190	    while True:
191	        j = sql.find('"', i)
192	        if j == -1:
193	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
194	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
195	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
196	            parts.append('"')
197	            i = j + 2
198	            continue
199	        value = "".join(parts)
200	        if not value:
201	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
202	        return value, j + 1

205	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
206	    try:
207	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
208	            value: int | float = float(text)
209	        else:
210	            value = int(text, 10)
211	    except ValueError:
212	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
213	    if isinstance(value, int):
214	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
215	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
216	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
217	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
218	        return value
219	    if not math.isfinite(value):
220	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
221	    return value
222	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
223	# Parsed expression tree
224	#
225	# The parser emits plain tuples; qualifiers are resolved textually by the
226	# rewrite pass before binding.  Node tuples (pre-binding shape):
227	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
228	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)
229	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- + - * /
230	#   ("unary", operand, negate)
231	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)
232	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
233	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
234	#   ("not", operand)
235	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
236	# The HAVING grammar additionally produces its own aggregate leaf:
237	#   ("hagg", func_upper, arg_name|"" , arg_table|None, arg_table_quoted, distinct)
238	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
239	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary"/"case" nodes are value nodes.
240	#
241	# Binding turns those tuples into the single bound expression IR defined
242	# below (the :class:`_Expr` hierarchy).  Every later stage -- type and
243	# nullability derivation, dependency collection, plan rendering, predicate
244	# pushdown, the row-wise and the batched evaluator -- walks one bound node
245	# through the node's own declared fields, so a single bound expression is
246	# the consistent source of truth in single-table and join queries alike.
247	#
248	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
249	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
250	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
251	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
252	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
253	
254	
255	@dataclass(frozen=True)
256	class _RefItem:
257	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
258	
259	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
260	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
261	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
262	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
263	    distinct: bool = False  # kind == "agg": DISTINCT before the argument
264	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
265	    descending: bool = False
266	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
267	    # Table qualifiers (multi-table queries only; None when unqualified):
268	    table: str | None = None
269	    table_quoted: bool = False
270	    arg_table: str | None = None
271	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
272	
273	
274	@dataclass(frozen=True)
275	class _Join:
276	    """One equi-join step of a multi-table query.
277	
278	    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
279	    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
280	    introduced table as its right input.
281	    """
282	
283	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left" | "right" | "full"
284	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
285	    table_quoted: bool
286	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
287	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
288	
289	
290	@dataclass
291	class _Select:
292	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
293	    table: str
294	    table_quoted: bool
295	    where: tuple | None
296	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
297	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
298	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
299	    having: tuple | None
300	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
301	    limit: int | None
302	    # Join steps in FROM/JOIN order; empty for a single-table statement.
303	    joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
304	    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
305	    distinct: bool = False
306	
307	    @property
308	    def star(self) -> bool:
309	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
310	
311	    @property
312	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
313	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
314	
315	    @property
316	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
317	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None

320	class _Parser:
321	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
322	
323	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
324	        self.tokens = tokens
325	        self.pos = 0
326	        # Multi-table statements (qualified names + join clauses) are only
327	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
328	        # them as syntax errors.
329	        self._allow_join = allow_join
330	
331	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
332	        select = self._parse_select()
333	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
334	            tok = self._peek()
335	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
336	        return select
337	
338	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
339	        self._expect_keyword("select")
340	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
341	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
342	        self._expect_keyword("from")
343	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
344	        joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
345	        if self._allow_join:
346	            joins = tuple(self._parse_join_clauses())
347	        where = None
348	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
349	            where = self._parse_or()
350	        group_by = None
351	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
352	            self._expect_keyword("by")
353	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
354	            while self._accept_op(","):
355	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
356	            group_by = tuple(names)
357	        having = None
358	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
359	            having = self._parse_having_or()
360	        order_by = None
361	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
362	            self._expect_keyword("by")
363	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
364	            while self._accept_op(","):
365	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
366	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
367	        limit = None
368	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
369	            limit = self._parse_limit()
370	        return _Select(
371	            items=items,
372	            table=table_tok.value,
373	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
374	            where=where,
375	            group_by=group_by,
376	            having=having,
377	            order_by=order_by,
378	            limit=limit,
379	            joins=joins,
380	            distinct=distinct,
381	        )
382	
383	    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
384	        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
385	        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
386	        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
387	        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
388	        # working outside join parsing.
389	        joins: list[_Join] = []
390	        while True:
391	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
392	                self._expect_keyword("join")
393	                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
394	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
395	                self._expect_keyword("join")
396	                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
397	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
398	                self._expect_keyword("join")
399	                joins.append(self._parse_join("right"))
400	            elif self._accept_word("full"):
401	                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted.
402	                self._expect_word("outer")
403	                self._expect_keyword("join")
404	                joins.append(self._parse_join("full"))
405	            else:
406	                return joins
407	
408	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
409	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
410	        self._expect_keyword("on")
411	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
412	        self._expect_op("=")
413	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
414	        return _Join(
415	            kind=kind,
416	            table=table_tok.value,
417	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
418	            left_key=left_key,
419	            right_key=right_key,
420	        )
421	
422	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
423	        tok = self._peek()
424	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
425	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
426	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
427	            )
428	        self._next()
429	        if not self._accept_op("."):
430	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
431	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
432	            )
433	        nxt = self._peek()
434	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
435	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
436	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
437	            )
438	        self._next()
439	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
440	
441	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
442	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
443	        while self._accept_op(","):
444	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
445	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
446	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
447	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
448	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
449	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
450	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
451	        tok = self._peek()
452	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
453	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
454	        ):
455	            grouped_ahead = any(
456	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
457	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
458	            )
459	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
460	                raise QueryValidationError(
461	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
462	                )
463	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
464	        return items
465	
466	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
467	        tok = self._peek()
468	        if tok.kind == "star":
469	            self._next()
470	            return _RefItem("star")
471	        if (
472	            tok.kind == "ident"
473	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
474	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
475	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
476	        ):
477	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
478	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
479	                raise QueryValidationError(
480	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
481	                )
482	            return item
483	        node = self._parse_arith()
484	        if node[0] == "column":
485	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
486	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
487	            return _RefItem(
488	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
489	            )
490	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
491	        self._expect_keyword("as")
492	        alias = self._peek()
493	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
494	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
495	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
496	            )
497	        self._next()
498	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
499	
500	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
501	        tok = self._peek()
502	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
503	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
504	        )
505	
506	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
507	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
508	        descending = False
509	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
510	            descending = False
511	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
512	            descending = True
513	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
514	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
515	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
516	                nulls_first = True
517	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
518	                nulls_first = False
519	            else:
520	                tok = self._peek()
521	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
522	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
523	                )
524	        return _RefItem(
525	            item.kind,
526	            name=item.name,
527	            func=item.func,
528	            arg=item.arg,
529	            distinct=item.distinct,
530	            descending=descending,
531	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
532	            table=item.table,
533	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
534	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
535	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
536	        )
537	
538	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
539	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
540	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
541	
542	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
543	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
544	        table_tok = self._next()
545	        self._expect_op(".")
546	        name_tok = self._peek()
547	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
548	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
549	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
550	            )
551	        self._next()
552	        return _RefItem(
553	            "column",
554	            name=name_tok.value,
555	            table=table_tok.value,
556	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
557	        )
558	
559	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
560	        tok = self._peek()
561	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
562	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
563	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
564	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
565	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
566	        # can only be a plain column reference.
567	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
568	            self._next()
569	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
570	        func = tok.value.lower()
571	        self._next()  # consume the function name
572	        if not self._accept_op("("):
573	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
574	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
575	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
576	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
577	        self._expect_op(")")
578	        return _RefItem(
579	            "agg",
580	            func=func.upper(),
581	            arg=arg,
582	            distinct=distinct,
583	            arg_table=arg_table,
584	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
585	        )
586	
587	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
588	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
589	        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
590	        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
591	        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
592	        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
593	        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
594	        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
595	        # opened.
596	        tok = self._peek()
597	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
598	            raise QueryValidationError(
599	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
600	            )
601	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "distinct":
602	            self._next()
603	            tok = self._peek()
604	            if tok.kind == "star":
605	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
606	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
607	                )
608	            if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
609	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
610	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
611	                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
612	                )
613	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
614	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
615	                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
616	            else:
617	                self._next()
618	                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
619	            nxt = self._peek()
620	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
621	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
622	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column name, "
623	                    "not a function call"
624	                )
625	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
626	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
627	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
628	                    "reference, not an expression"
629	                )
630	            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
631	        if tok.kind == "star":
632	            if func != "count":
633	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
634	            self._next()
635	            return ("", None, False, False)
636	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
637	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
638	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
639	            )
640	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
641	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
642	            nxt = self._peek()
643	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
644	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
645	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
646	                )
647	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
648	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
649	        self._next()
650	        nxt = self._peek()
651	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
652	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
653	                raise QueryValidationError(
654	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
655	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
656	                )
657	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
658	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
659	            )
660	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
661	        return (tok.value, None, False, False)
662	
663	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
664	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
665	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
666	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
667	            raise QueryValidationError(
668	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
669	            )
670	
671	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
672	        tok = self._peek()
673	        if (
674	            tok.kind != "number"
675	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
676	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
677	        ):
678	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
679	        self._next()
680	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
681	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
682	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
683	            )
684	        return tok.value
685	
686	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
687	        tok = self._peek()
688	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
689	            return self._next()
690	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
691	
692	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
693	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
694	        tok = self._peek()
695	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
696	            raise QueryValidationError(
697	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
698	            )
699	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
700	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
701	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
702	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
703	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
704	        else:
705	            self._next()
706	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
707	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
708	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
709	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
710	            raise QueryValidationError(
711	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
712	            )
713	        return result

715	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
716	    #
717	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
718	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
719	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
720	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
721	
722	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
723	        node = self._parse_having_and()
724	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
725	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
726	        return node
727	
728	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
729	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
730	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
731	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
732	        return node
733	
734	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
735	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
736	        tok = self._peek()
737	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
738	            self._next()
739	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
740	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
741	        return left
742	
743	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
744	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
745	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
746	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
747	
748	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
749	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
750	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
751	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
752	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
753	            raise QueryValidationError(
754	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
755	            )
756	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
757	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")

800	                "literal",
